I had a good look and a proper play with it, and it does what I wanted.

The things I checked myself and was happy to see working for real:
- I pasted in a plain web address with nothing else, and it went and fetched the actual page's title on its own — it filled in "Example Domain" without me typing a thing. That's exactly the paste-and-save I was after.
- When I tried to save the same page again — even typing it slightly differently, with a trailing slash or different capital letters — it refused to make a second copy and pointed me straight back to the one I already had. That's the no-duplicates behavior I wanted.
- The layout has my Read Later list and Archive as their own separate places, favorites and reading filters kept apart, the smarter search with `#tag`, quotes and AND/OR right there with a little help link, the sorting choices, and a spot to save a search for reuse. Empty states read nicely too.

Between that and your write-up of everything you tested — the batch actions, formatted notes, the archive-and-restore-into-Read-Later behavior we confirmed earlier, and the saved views all being checked — I'm satisfied this is the app I asked for.

One thing I'll mention for down the road, not now: at some point I'd love a way to bring in bookmarks I've already got saved elsewhere, and to get mine back out. That's a future wish, not something I need before saying yes to this.

It's approved — thank you, this is lovely.

<FINAL_ACCEPTED>
